lead.title: Anthropic's Claude designs protein binders against scorpion toxins — all data open-sourced
lead.summary: Anthropic had Claude generate over 300,000 candidate protein binders for five scorpion neurotoxins in 64 hours; 211 were synthesized and lab-tested with Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience, 17 of which bound their targets. The full dataset and technical report were released on Hugging Face.

top_stories.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its production services
top_stories.summary: DeepSeek released DeepInfer on GitHub under Apache 2.0, describing it as the high-performance inference framework powering its large-scale production services. It targets DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and supports Nvidia SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs.

top_stories.title: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio to advance Rosalind AI for drug development
top_stories.summary: OpenAI announced the acquisition of Orchestra Bio, a platform coordinating complex biopharma drug development workflows, with the founding team joining. It will be integrated with Rosalind, OpenAI's life-sciences AI stack, to accelerate bringing treatments to patients.

top_stories.title: Mistral ships Voxtral 3, a new open speech model family
top_stories.summary: Mistral released Voxtral 3, the next generation of its Voxtral speech model family, days after launching Timestral time-series models. The release drew a large Hacker News response (569 points).

top_stories.title: Cloudflare ports TypeScript to Rust with 'Tsrs'
top_stories.summary: Cloudflare published a port of TypeScript to Rust, which landed on the Hacker News front page with 374 points. The project targets performance-critical TypeScript tooling.

items.title: When Do LLMs Help with Feature Selection? A Systematic Empirical Study
items.summary: LLMs can leverage semantic feature names and summary statistics for tabular feature selection, yet it remains unclear when such information improves subset selection relative to established statistical methods. An 18-dataset framework examines this.

items.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
items.summary: A roadmap for next-generation Matrix-Game that separates game execution from visual generation through an executable game harness, with Matrix-Game 4.0 as the first system built on this design.

items.title: When LLMs Manipulate: Measuring Behavioral, Social, and Temporal Effects
items.summary: A behavioral computing framework for measuring 'behavioral vulnerability' — users' susceptibility to manipulative AI responses — as LLMs influence trust and decision-making through subtle linguistic cues.

items.title: SGLang ships Low-Latency Mode built with NVIDIA and AMD — big speedups on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
items.summary: LMSYS announced SGLang Low-Latency Mode: on GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash goes from 671 to 928 tok/s (1.38x P90 per-user speed in agentic traces); on AMD MI355X from 332 to 516 tok/s (1.56x). Kernel overlapping on NVIDIA and persistent kernels on AMD, plus a new plugin system. Low-latency kernels for GLM-5.3, K3, and MiniMax M3 are next.

items.title: SGLang-Omni: full-duplex real-time multimodal interaction with strong latency numbers
items.summary: LMSYS shared SGLang-Omni, work on full-duplex / real-time multimodal interaction. On a Qwen3.8-27B cascade it reports 0.17s stop latency and 1.32s response latency on a single H200.

items.title: MemT-1.0 memory-native LLMs claim 66x KV-storage reduction at 128K tokens
items.summary: A new foundation-model release bakes memory into the model itself instead of carrying a full KV cache, cutting 128K-token serving storage by roughly 66x. It ships Nano (36B) and Flash (288B) variants built on Qwen3.6 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash backbones.

items.title: Eka is worth $1.45B thanks to a physical AI model that has experts raving
items.summary: Eka Robotics raised $150M Series A at a $1.45B valuation for its vision-force-action physical AI robot model, in a round led by a16z and F-Prime. The model is aimed at enabling robots to perform physical tasks in real-world environments.

items.title: JR West's Railway Robots Wield Huge Chainsaws
items.summary: West Japan Railway is expanding its ZIZAI program with two teleoperated maintenance machines, the single-arm ZX-2 and dual-arm ZX-3, for live railway infrastructure work including overhead lines and tree cutting. Deployment on operational rail lines is scheduled for October and November 2026.

items.title: UniX AI Shows Panther for Facility Patrol
items.summary: UniX AI presented its Panther wheeled dual-arm humanoid for 24/7 facility patrol, highlighting multimodal perception and adaptive manipulation for unstructured sites. Panther is a full-size omnidirectional four-wheel humanoid with 8-DoF bionic arms rated for roughly 12 kg per arm.

items.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch back end for TPUs
items.summary: Google released TorchTPU on GitHub, a native PyTorch back end for TPU hardware. The open-sourcing simplifies PyTorch workloads on Google's TPU infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI spotlights Terminal X, an agentic research platform built on GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI published a case study on Terminal X, whose agent workflow runs on GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna and is claimed to match senior investor judgment 88.6% of the time. It includes an Eval Agent that grades agent output against the firm's standards.

items.title: Spotify launches paid podcast memberships with perks beyond bonus content
items.summary: Spotify launched paid podcast memberships in 34 markets, letting creators offer perks like fewer ads and early access across multiple tiers while keeping 90% of revenue. Qualifying shows must host on Spotify for Creators or Megaphone.

items.title: Devs use Claude Code and DeepSeek to strip ads from smart TVs
items.summary: Two open-source GitHub projects — cleanyourtv and dumbtv — use AI coding agents to remove ads, trackers, and bloatware from smart TVs. dumbtv was built with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Claude models and tested on Fire TV and Android/Google TV hardware.

items.title: EN 18286 Published in Official Gazette: First Harmonized Standard Under the EU AI Act
items.summary: EN 18286, the first harmonized standard of the EU AI Act, has been published in the Italian Gazzetta Ufficiale. It grants a conformity presumption for quality management systems under Article 17, but accuracy, robustness, data and cybersecurity remain outside its scope.

items.title: AI Act Compliance Guide: A 7-Point Checklist for Italian SMEs
items.summary: AI4Business published a seven-point compliance checklist to help Italian SMEs classify AI systems, verify prohibitions, apply transparency and content-marking rules, and document compliance ahead of the AI Act deadlines.
